literature_notes: Three ledger lines were evaluated. L1 and L2 both describe the same pCMV3-mLINGO3-GFP construct expressed in HEK293 cells. The naming convention 'LINGO3-GFP' (protein-GFP) and the pCMV3 vector architecture indicate a C-terminal GFP fusion. LINGO3 is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein (N-out, C-in): extracellular 25–526, TM 527–549, intracellular 550–592. A C-terminal GFP therefore sits in the intracellular compartment (after residue 592) and is not a surface tag. The flow-cytometry result demonstrates that the full-length protein reaches the cell surface and that its extracellular domain binds TFF2 ligand, but the GFP reporter itself is not extracellularly exposed. This construct is recorded in other_positions. L3 describes a 'Flag-tagged LINGO3' used in CHO-cell co-immunoprecipitation experiments. The ledger clip does not state whether the Flag tag is at the N-terminus (which would be extracellular after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 24) or the C-terminus (which would be intracellular). Co-IP from cell lysate is compatible with either orientation, so the clip provides no evidence that the Flag is on the extracellular face. The tag position is unstated; insert_after_residue cannot be pinned; the topology-derived rule does not apply because surface localisation of the tag itself is not confirmed. L3 therefore does not qualify any surface site. No ledger line supports a tag insertion on the extracellular face of LINGO3 at a pinnable position.

literature_other_positions.note: LINGO3-GFP (pCMV3-mLINGO3-GFP) is a C-terminal GFP fusion; for this type I TM protein (C-terminus intracellular, residues 550–592) the GFP tag is cytoplasmic, not surface-exposed.
